what_was_wrong: Dropped negation. The Marathi contains नाही (not); the English rendered it as the positive 'very difficult' — the exact opposite of what the learner must produce.
prereq_evidence: difficult introduced S66 ('It's not difficult to find the answer'); very/खूप introduced well before S66; negation नाही attested S66. No new material.
marathi_basis: IN-COURSE, same seed. S0149 seed text 'हे फारसं अवघड नाही' is rendered 'This isn't very difficult' by the course itself, and five USE phrases on this lego already render the identical Marathi with the negation. S66 independently attests अवघड नाही = 'not difficult'. फारसं…नाही is the standard Marathi 'not very / not much' frame. Marathi side UNCHANGED — only the English is corrected.
notes: Marathi untouched, so the known clip re-links automatically; only the two English clips are new.

what_was_wrong: Dropped negation AND a glued tag: 'already' cannot attach to a bare adjectival fragment, and आधीच is likewise bolted onto the end of the Marathi.
prereq_evidence: difficult S66; ते ('that') attested from the earliest seeds. No new material.
marathi_basis: IN-COURSE, same seed: USE phrase S0149L02U02 is 'ते फारसं अवघड नाही, त्यामुळे…' rendered 'that isn't very difficult so…'. The demonstrative ते is neuter, agreeing with the neuter reading of the clause — same form the seed uses.

what_was_wrong: Dropped negation AND a glued tag. 'soon' was an attempt to combine this lego with L1 ('soon'/लवकरच); the two do not combine into English, and लवकरच is simply appended in the Marathi.
prereq_evidence: difficult S66; 'today'/आज introduced long before S149 (it is a lego by S114 and appears far earlier). No new material.
marathi_basis: Chunk फारसं अवघड नाही is unchanged and in-course attested. आज is placed CLAUSE-INITIALLY, which is the position the course's own well-formed sentences use for time adverbs (S0114 seed: 'मी कालपेक्षा आज जास्त वाईट करतोय'); the broken original appended it after the negator instead. I am confident about the words; I am slightly less confident that a bare time-adverb fragment reads as naturally in Marathi as it does in English.
notes: EXPLICIT GAP: adverb placement here is grounded in in-course word order, not in an external Marathi grammar reference. A speaker may prefer 'आज हे फारसं अवघड नाही'.
